about: TurkuNLP is a group of about 30 researchers at the University of Turku, ranging from research assistants to professors. Its main topics are syntactic and semantic analysis of Finnish, large language models for Finnish and other languages, biomedical and clinical text mining, and the analysis of internet registers and genres.

The group's resources include FinBERT, WikiBERT, FinGPT and the Turku Dependency Treebank. With Silo AI's SiloGen it built the Poro and Viking models on the LUMI supercomputer; Viking, released in 2024 in 7B, 13B and 33B sizes, covers the Nordic languages, English and code under Apache 2.0.
TurkuNLP co-hosts an open monthly seminar on NLP and AI with Omni Language AI Research, and publishes its code and models on GitHub and Hugging Face.

about: UCL DARK (Deciding, Acting, and Reasoning with Knowledge) was a research group at University College London led by Tim Rocktäschel, working on reinforcement learning, open-endedness and the safety of language models.

Edward Grefenstette was an honorary professor and Roberta Raileanu and Jack Parker-Holder honorary lecturers. Alumni include researchers now at Google DeepMind, Anthropic and the UK AI Security Institute.
The group's website now reports that DARK has been merged into the BOLD Lab. Its research code remains on GitHub.

about: The Ubiquitous Knowledge Processing Lab belongs to the Department of Computer Science at TU Darmstadt and was founded by Iryna Gurevych. Its early work covered information retrieval, question answering and the structured use of wikis, including the Java Wikipedia Library and Java Wiktionary Library.

It created Sentence-BERT, the basis of the Sentence Transformers library, with Nils Reimers in 2019, and develops AdapterHub. In October 2025 maintenance of Sentence Transformers passed to Hugging Face under Apache 2.0.
VITA, the Visual Intelligence for Transportation lab, is led by Alexandre Alahi at EPFL, where he joined in 2017. It works on socially aware AI for safe autonomous systems and mobility.

Its open code includes OpenPifPaf for human pose estimation, which was combined with commercial licensing for technology transfer, along with trajectory prediction and video generation projects on GitHub.

about: Upstage was founded in October 2020 by Sung Kim, a former professor at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology who previously led Naver's Clova team. It builds language models and document AI for enterprises.
Its compact Solar 10.7B model was released in December 2023, followed by Solar Pro 2 in July 2025. Some models are published openly, though later releases are under the Upstage Solar License.
